newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico debtors' leader sues for rights violations.
newsitem.headline: Mexico debtors' leader sues for rights violations.

text.p: The leader of a middle-class debtors' group said on Wednesday he was suing a Mexican state for wrongfully imprisoning him and fabricating charges when he tried to protest at a bankers' convention.
Authorities rolled out the red carpet last week for 1,000 international bankers attending the glitzy annual Mexican Banking Convention in the Caribbean resort of Cancun.

Gerardo Fernandez Norona, leader of the Citizens Assembly of Bank Debtors, said his group had its hotel reservations cancelled, its members tailed by detectives and nine organisers arrested on the convention's first day last Friday.

"Today I am presenting an accusation against the state prosecutor for kidnapping," Fernandez Norona said by telephone from Cancun after his release on bail on Tuesday from a jail where he said he was held with murderers and drug dealers.

"This is a barbarity ... the evidence against us is totally fabricated," he added. "The government is desperate, intolerant and repressive. It is responding to our fair demands with violence -- but that won't stop people from disagreeing."

Fernandez Norona said he and other leaders were tailed by judical police and Interior Ministry agents from the moment they arrived in Cancun for a legal forum they had planned on how to win court cases against the banks.
But the forum was called off after three hotels in succession cancelled the group's paid reservations and refused to let them in, he said.

Mario Villanueva, governor of the state of Quintana Roo which includes Cancun, said the debtors' group leaders had been arrested because they had made bomb threats against the banking convention and planned to "cause destabilisation in Cancun".

"Cancun is a very tranquil place and we're not going to let someone come and disturb the peace because he doesn't agree about something with the banks," he said. Asked whether any bombs were found, Villanueva said, "Fortunately, no".

Local reporters said state prosecutors had dropped the bomb hoax charge against Fernandez Norona and were now accusing him of beating up the police who arrested him at a road block as he travelled to the convention last Friday.
No charges were filed against six of the group's organisers, who were detained for more than 10 hours last Friday.
Villanueva had given a news conference last Saturday saying the men would be charged with "telephone terrorism."
There was no official explanation for the contradictions in the allegations against the debtors' group and state officials could not be reached for comment.

The Citizens Assembly is an 8,000-strong group of debtors who started protesting after Mexico's 1994-1995 economic crisis left them with sky-high debt interest payments they say they cannot afford to pay.
